title: Regular Expression Matching
description: Brute force to optimized: unmemoized recursive exploration of star branches versus a 2D bottom-up DP grid.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given a string s and a pattern p containing "." (matches any single character) and "*" (matches zero or more of the PRECEDING element), implement regular expression matching that covers the ENTIRE string s (not just a partial match).

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","s, pattern p"],["Output","true if p matches all of s"],["Key Insight","A pattern character followed by \"*\" can either be skipped entirely (zero occurrences) or consume one matching s character while staying at the same pattern position (to allow repeating)"],["Constraints","Up to 20 characters each"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Full-string pattern matching with wildcard-like repetition\"","The classic 2D string-matching DP: dp[i][j] tracks whether s's first i characters match pattern's first j characters, with a special branching rule for \"*\""]]}

blocks.text: Define dp[i][j] as true if the first i characters of s match the first j characters of pattern. If pattern[j-1] is a normal character or ".", it must directly match s[i-1] (or be "."), extending dp[i-1][j-1]. If pattern[j-1] is "*", it refers to the character BEFORE it, and there are two options: use ZERO occurrences of that preceding character (skip both it and the "*", checking dp[i][j-2]), or, if that preceding character matches s[i-1] (or is "."), use ONE MORE occurrence, checking dp[i-1][j] (staying at the same pattern position, since "*" can match many characters).

blocks.title: Analogy: A Stamp That Can Be Used Zero, One, or Many Times in a Row
blocks.text: Picture matching a document against a template where certain template elements are marked "repeatable" (usable zero, one, or many times in a row). At each point, either that repeatable element is skipped entirely, or one more repetition is consumed from the document while still allowing further repetitions afterward.

blocks.caption: A pattern-char-plus-star can be skipped (zero uses) or extended by one matching character (staying at the same pattern position)

blocks.text: Result: false (pattern "a" cannot cover the entire "aa").
Result: true ("a*" matches zero or more "a"s, covering "aa").
Result: true (".*" matches any sequence of any characters).

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: dp[0][0] is true (empty matches empty). dp[0][j] (empty s against a pattern prefix) can only be true if that prefix consists entirely of "x*" pairs each reducible to zero occurrences.

Observation 2: If pattern[j-1] is a normal character or ".", it must directly match s[i-1], extending dp[i-1][j-1] only if that direct match succeeds.

Observation 3: If pattern[j-1] is "*", dp[i][j] is true if EITHER dp[i][j-2] is true (use zero occurrences of the preceding element, skip both it and the star), OR the preceding pattern element matches s[i-1] (or is ".") AND dp[i-1][j] is true (use one more occurrence, staying at the same pattern position for potentially even more repetitions).

Observation 4: Filling this grid row by row (or via memoized recursion) builds up to dp[m][n], the final answer.
This leads to a 2D bottom-up DP grid, with a special branching rule wherever the pattern has a "*", combining a skip option and an extend option.
Recursively try both branches of a "*" (skip it, or consume one matching character and recurse without advancing the pattern), without memoization.
Why the code is written this way

items: Recursively trying both star branches directly implements the definition.
This recomputes the same (i, j) sub-positions repeatedly across different branches, costing exponential time; a 2D DP grid computes each sub-position exactly once.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: exponential without memoization, in the worst case.
Space: O(m+n) recursion depth.
Limitation: a 2D DP grid computes each (i, j) sub-position exactly once, reusing smaller sub-positions directly.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: Build a (m+1) by (n+1) boolean DP grid, with dp[0][0] = true. Fill dp[0][j] for patterns that could match an empty string (only possible via trailing "x*" pairs reducible to zero occurrences). For i from 1 to m and j from 1 to n: if pattern[j-1] is "*", set dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-2] (skip) OR (the preceding pattern element matches s[i-1] AND dp[i-1][j]) (extend); otherwise, if pattern[j-1] matches s[i-1] directly (equal or "."), set dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Return dp[m][n].
Use a 2D bottom-up DP grid, with a special branching rule (skip or extend) wherever the pattern has a "*".

blocks.content: {"headers":["Cell","Reasoning"],"rows":[["dp[0][0]","true, empty matches empty"],["dp[0][2] (\"a*\")","true, zero occurrences of \"a\""],["dp[1][2]","true, extend using dp[0][2] since \"a\" matches s[0]"],["dp[2][2] (final)","true, extend using dp[1][2] since \"a\" matches s[1]"]]}

blocks.text: For a normal pattern character (or "."), a direct match simply extends the diagonal sub-problem, exactly as expected. For a "*", correctly modeling BOTH possible uses, zero occurrences (skip, checking two positions back in the pattern) and one additional occurrence (extend, staying at the same pattern column while advancing s by one character), correctly captures every valid way the repeated element could account for zero or more matching characters, with the OR of these two branches giving the correct overall result at every cell.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(m times n).
Space: O(m times n), reducible to O(n) using a rolling row.

blocks.text: Regular Expression Matching is a hallmark hard 2D string DP problem, requiring careful handling of the "*" quantifier's two distinct possible uses (skip or extend).

items: Forgetting the "zero occurrences" (skip) branch of "*", handling only the "extend" branch and missing valid matches.
Incorrectly indexing the character BEFORE the "*" (at position j-2, not j-1) when checking if it matches the current s character.

blocks.text: Explicitly stating "a star has two uses: use it zero times (skip), or use it one more time (extend, staying at the same pattern position)" is the exact recurrence to communicate precisely.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "regular expression matching with wildcard characters and repetition", think: 2D DP with a special skip-or-extend branch for the "*" quantifier.

Wildcard Matching, a very closely related problem using "?" and "*" with slightly different (simpler) semantics.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The unmemoized recursive approach costs exponential time in the worst case; the 2D DP grid costs O(m times n), the standard efficient solution.

items: Pattern: 2D bottom-up dynamic programming with a special skip-or-extend branch for the "*" quantifier.
Core Idea: a "*" can be used zero times (skip two pattern positions back) or one more time (extend, staying at the same pattern position).
Time: exponential worst case for the brute force, O(m times n) for the DP approach.
Space: O(m+n) recursion depth for the brute force, O(m times n) (reducible to O(n)) for the DP approach.
Most Important Observation: "*" always refers to the SINGLE character immediately preceding it in the pattern.
Interview Difficulty: a very challenging, classic hard-tier DP problem.
One line memory trick: star means skip it, or use one more and stay put.
